_meta.source: English Appendix 1: Spelling (UK National Curriculum, DfE 2013, Crown Copyright)
_meta.license_note: Statutory word lists reused under the Open Government Licence.
_meta.purpose: Chapter-structured wordbank for the Hangman spelling game (11+ preparation).
_meta.schema_notes: Each word is now an object with fields: word, ipa, meaning {partOfSpeech, definition, example}, image. Meanings and IPA are embedded so the app needs no dictionary API at runtime. Image is the filename the app expects in assets/images/. v4 adds 'chunks': an array of 1-4 letter spelling chunks. Used by the Spell-Aloud feature to teach pronunciation chunk by chunk. Most chunks come from pyphen British English syllabification; single-syllable and pedagogically tricky words use manual overrides.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 — Double letters

chapters.title: Chapter 5 — Common but tricky
chapters.description: 11 words to practise.

meaning.definition: A place where books are kept that you can borrow.
meaning.example: I go to the library to borrow books.

meaning.definition: To say something briefly.
meaning.example: Did she mention the party to you?

meaning.definition: Made by nature, not by people.
meaning.example: Wood is a natural material.

meaning.definition: Maybe.
meaning.example: Perhaps it will snow tomorrow.

meaning.definition: Liked by many people.
meaning.example: Football is a popular sport.

meaning.definition: To say you will definitely do something.
meaning.example: I promise to tidy my room.

meaning.definition: The reason something is done.
meaning.example: The purpose of a hat is to keep your head warm.

meaning.definition: Happening often at the same times.
meaning.example: I do regular exercise after school.

meaning.definition: Different from the usual; better than ordinary.
meaning.example: Today is a special day because it is my birthday.

meaning.definition: The details of where someone lives or where a building is.
meaning.example: Please write your address on the envelope.

meaning.definition: Took hold of something that was moving (past tense of catch).
meaning.example: She caught the ball with one hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Longer everyday words
chapters.description: 11 words to practise.

meaning.definition: Number 8 in a list or order.
meaning.example: August is the eighth month of the year.

meaning.definition: How tall something is.
meaning.example: What is the height of the tree?

meaning.definition: To have or own something.
meaning.example: She does not possess a mobile phone.

meaning.definition: Used to add a different idea (similar to 'but').
meaning.example: I will come, though I might be late.

meaning.definition: How heavy something is.
meaning.example: Weigh the flour to find its weight.

meaning.definition: To reach a place.
meaning.example: We will arrive at the station at six o'clock.

meaning.definition: A chart that shows all the days, weeks and months of the year.
meaning.example: I marked my birthday on the calendar.

meaning.definition: Finished; with nothing missing.
meaning.example: My homework is complete.

meaning.definition: To think carefully about something.
meaning.example: Please consider my idea before saying no.

meaning.definition: To keep doing something; to go on.
meaning.example: Continue reading until the end of the page.

meaning.definition: To say what something or someone is like.
meaning.example: Can you describe the man you saw?

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — More syllables, more care
chapters.description: 11 words to practise.

meaning.definition: The second month of the year.
meaning.example: Valentine's Day is in February.

meaning.definition: To become bigger or more.
meaning.example: The number of pupils will increase next year.

meaning.definition: A feeling of wanting to know more about something.
meaning.example: She has an interest in dinosaurs.

meaning.definition: What something is made of, like wood, cloth or plastic.
meaning.example: Wool is a warm material for jumpers.

meaning.definition: Strange or unusual.
meaning.example: The soup had a peculiar smell.

meaning.definition: Vegetables that grow under the ground; can be roasted, mashed or chipped.
meaning.example: We had roast potatoes for dinner.

meaning.definition: Very likely.
meaning.example: It will probably rain later.

meaning.definition: To bring something back into your mind.
meaning.example: Remember to take your packed lunch.

meaning.definition: A group of words that makes complete sense.
meaning.example: Begin a sentence with a capital letter.

meaning.definition: Something unexpected.
meaning.example: The birthday cake was a lovely surprise.

meaning.definition: An idea in your mind.
meaning.example: A funny thought made her giggle.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Spotting the traps
chapters.description: 11 words to practise.

meaning.definition: From one side to the other.
meaning.example: The train went through the tunnel.

meaning.definition: Mattering a lot.
meaning.example: It is important to brush your teeth.

meaning.definition: To think something might be true.
meaning.example: I suppose he might be late.

meaning.definition: Something bad that happens by mistake, not on purpose.
meaning.example: She had a small accident and dropped the glass.

meaning.definition: In fact; really.
meaning.example: I thought it was sunny but actually it was raining.

meaning.definition: The work of buying and selling things; a company.
meaning.example: Her family runs a small bakery business.

meaning.definition: A force pushing on something.
meaning.example: Air pressure can make balloons pop.

meaning.definition: To make a picture of something in your mind.
meaning.example: Imagine you could fly anywhere.

meaning.definition: Not the same.
meaning.example: These two shoes are different colours.

meaning.definition: Not easy; hard to do.
meaning.example: This puzzle is difficult but fun.

meaning.definition: To stop being seen; to go out of sight.
meaning.example: The magician made the rabbit disappear.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — Real challenge
chapters.description: 11 words to practise.

meaning.definition: As much as is needed.
meaning.example: We have enough food for everyone.

meaning.definition: Activity that makes your body or mind work to keep it healthy.
meaning.example: Running is good exercise.

meaning.definition: Something you take to feel better when you are ill.
meaning.example: The doctor gave me some medicine for my cough.

meaning.definition: Normal; nothing special.
meaning.example: It was just an ordinary Tuesday.

meaning.definition: The place where someone or something is.
meaning.example: Stand in your position on the field.

meaning.definition: Something you ask when you want to know an answer.
meaning.example: Put up your hand if you have a question.

meaning.definition: Apart from each other; not together.
meaning.example: Put the red socks in a separate pile.

meaning.definition: Not behaving well.
meaning.example: The naughty puppy chewed my slippers.

meaning.definition: The one you like best.
meaning.example: Pizza is my favourite food.

meaning.definition: All the things you know.
meaning.example: Reading books gives you lots of knowledge.

meaning.definition: For that reason.
meaning.example: It was raining, therefore we stayed inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 — Toughest of all
chapters.description: 10 words to practise.

meaning.definition: Even though; in spite of the fact that.
meaning.example: Although it was cold, we still played outside.

meaning.definition: Something that happens to you; knowledge from doing things.
meaning.example: Going on holiday was a great experience.

meaning.definition: A test to find out what happens; often used in science.
meaning.example: We did an experiment with magnets in class.

meaning.definition: A special time when something happens.
meaning.example: A wedding is a happy occasion.

meaning.definition: Completely different from something.
meaning.example: Hot is the opposite of cold.

meaning.definition: One special one rather than any other.
meaning.example: I want this particular pen, not the other one.

meaning.definition: Able to happen or be done.
meaning.example: It is possible to learn anything.

meaning.definition: Something you own.
meaning.example: His favourite possession is his old teddy bear.

meaning.definition: Not on purpose; by mistake.
meaning.example: He accidentally stepped on the cat's tail.

meaning.definition: Sometimes, but not often.
meaning.example: We occasionally go to the seaside.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Un-, dis- and mis-
chapters.description: Adding un-, dis- or mis- to the start of a word changes its meaning, and the rest of the word stays the same, as in our examples.

meaning.definition: Not kind; mean or hurtful to other people.
meaning.example: It is unkind to laugh at someone who has fallen.

meaning.definition: Not right or equal; not treating everyone the same.
meaning.example: It felt unfair that only one team got a prize.

meaning.definition: Messy; not neat.
meaning.example: Her untidy bedroom had toys all over the floor.

meaning.definition: To open something using a key.
meaning.example: Dad used a key to unlock the shed.

meaning.definition: To not enjoy or care for something.
meaning.example: I dislike cold porridge but I love toast.

meaning.definition: To think differently from someone else.
meaning.example: We disagree about which film to watch tonight.

meaning.definition: To spell a word without getting the letters right.
meaning.example: Check your work so you do not misspell any words.

meaning.definition: To give someone a false idea so they believe something untrue.
meaning.example: Muddled signs can mislead people on a walk.

meaning.definition: Not telling the truth; likely to cheat or lie.
meaning.example: A dishonest player hid the card up his sleeve.

meaning.definition: To act badly or not follow the rules.
meaning.example: The puppy tends to misbehave when visitors arrive.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — Re-, sub- and super-
chapters.description: The prefixes re- (again), sub- (under) and super- (above or very big) are added to a whole word, as in our examples.

meaning.definition: To play something again.
meaning.example: Can we replay that funny video one more time?

meaning.definition: To make food hot again.
meaning.example: Mum will reheat the soup for lunch.

meaning.definition: To write something again, often to make it better.
meaning.example: I will rewrite my story with a new ending.

meaning.definition: To build something again.
meaning.example: We helped rebuild the sandcastle after the wave hit it.

meaning.definition: A path or tunnel under a road or the ground.
meaning.example: We walked through the subway to cross the busy road.

meaning.definition: A very famous and brilliant singer, player or performer.
meaning.example: The football superstar signed shirts for the fans.

meaning.definition: To take one number away from another.
meaning.example: You subtract four from nine to get five.

meaning.definition: A character with amazing powers who helps people.
meaning.example: My favourite superhero can fly high above the city.

meaning.definition: A ship that can travel underwater.
meaning.example: The submarine dived deep beneath the waves.

meaning.definition: A big shop that sells food and many other things.
meaning.example: We buy our fruit at the supermarket.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Adding -ly
chapters.description: Adding -ly turns a describing word into one that says how something is done; words ending in y change to -ily and words ending in -ic add -ally, as in our examples.

meaning.definition: In a soft, kind and careful way.
meaning.example: She gently stroked the sleepy kitten.

meaning.definition: At a fast speed.
meaning.example: She quickly put on her coat and ran outside.

meaning.definition: In a glad and cheerful way.
meaning.example: The children played happily in the park.

meaning.definition: Without trouble or hard work.
meaning.example: He lifted the small box easily.

meaning.definition: In a loud way that makes a lot of sound.
meaning.example: The geese honked noisily by the pond.

meaning.definition: In a cross way, showing you are very annoyed.
meaning.example: He stamped angrily when the tower fell down.

meaning.definition: In the most important ways; mostly.
meaning.example: A tomato is basically a fruit.

meaning.definition: In a way that seems done by magic.
meaning.example: The rabbit magically appeared from the hat.

meaning.definition: In a wonderful, amazing way.
meaning.example: The team played fantastically in the final.

meaning.definition: In a sudden and exciting way.
meaning.example: The sky dramatically darkened before the storm.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — Words ending -ation
chapters.description: The ending -ation sounds like 'shun' and is spelt a-t-i-o-n, as in our examples.

meaning.definition: A country and all its people.
meaning.example: The whole nation cheered when the team won.

meaning.definition: A gift of money or things to help others.
meaning.example: We gave a donation to the school fair.

meaning.definition: Something new that someone has made.
meaning.example: Her clay creation was shown at school.

meaning.definition: Travelling through a place to find out about it.
meaning.example: Our exploration of the woods found a hidden stream.

meaning.definition: A request to come to a party or event.
meaning.example: I got an invitation to a birthday party.

meaning.definition: Something pretty used to make a place look nice.
meaning.example: A paper star was the best decoration on the tree.

meaning.definition: Learning and teaching, usually at school.
meaning.example: Education helps us learn new things every day.

meaning.definition: Facts or details about something.
meaning.example: The sign gave information about the bus times.

meaning.definition: A special event to enjoy a happy day.
meaning.example: There was a big celebration at the school fair.

meaning.definition: The ability to picture new things in your mind.
meaning.example: Her imagination turned the box into a rocket.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 — Odd ou and y
chapters.focus: ou for the u sound (young, touch) and y for the i sound (gym, myth)
chapters.description: In these words the letters ou make the short 'u' sound and the letter y makes the short 'i' sound, as in our examples.

meaning.definition: A room or hall with equipment for exercise.
meaning.example: We play games in the gym on rainy days.

meaning.definition: An old story about gods or heroes that is not true.
meaning.example: We read a Greek myth about a winged horse.

meaning.definition: Not old; having lived for only a short time.
meaning.example: A young lamb followed its mother across the field.

meaning.definition: To put your hand on something.
meaning.example: Please do not touch the hot oven.

meaning.definition: Twice as much or twice as many.
meaning.example: I would like a double scoop of ice cream.

meaning.definition: The child of your aunt or uncle.
meaning.example: My cousin came to stay for the weekend.

meaning.definition: A difficulty or problem.
meaning.example: We had trouble finding the way back to the car.

meaning.definition: A land with its own people and rules, like France.
meaning.example: Which country would you most like to visit?

meaning.definition: Something strange that nobody can explain yet.
meaning.example: The missing biscuits stayed a mystery all day.

meaning.definition: A shape with a flat base and sloping sides meeting at a point.
meaning.example: Long ago, people built a huge pyramid from stone.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 — In-, im-, il- and ir-
chapters.focus: in-, im-, il- and ir- meaning not
chapters.description: Our examples of words that start with in-, im-, il- or ir- to mean not, as in invisible.

meaning.definition: Not able to be seen.
meaning.example: The magician made the rabbit look invisible.

meaning.definition: Not having good manners.
meaning.example: It is impolite to talk with your mouth full.

meaning.definition: Not moving or doing anything much.
meaning.example: The sleepy cat stayed inactive all afternoon.

meaning.definition: Not happy to wait for something.
meaning.example: Mia grew impatient waiting for the bus.

meaning.definition: Not allowed by the law.
meaning.example: It is illegal to drive without a licence.

meaning.definition: Not perfect; having a small fault.
meaning.example: My drawing is imperfect, but I like it.

meaning.definition: Not able to happen or be done.
meaning.example: Flapping your arms to fly is impossible.

meaning.definition: Not following the usual pattern or shape.
meaning.example: The stone had an irregular shape.

meaning.definition: Not sensible; not following clear thinking.
meaning.example: Wearing a coat in a heatwave is illogical.

meaning.definition: Not careful or sensible about what you do.
meaning.example: Leaving the gate open was irresponsible.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 — Words ending -sure and -ture
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -sure or -ture, such as measure and picture.

meaning.definition: A drawing, painting or photograph.
meaning.example: She hung the picture on the wall.

meaning.definition: Plants, animals and the world outside that people have not made.
meaning.example: We walked through the woods to enjoy nature.

meaning.definition: The time that is still to come.
meaning.example: I want to be a vet in the future.

meaning.definition: To find out how big, long or heavy something is.
meaning.example: Please measure the table with a ruler.

meaning.definition: Gold, jewels or other valuable things.
meaning.example: The pirates buried the treasure on the island.

meaning.definition: A feeling of happiness and enjoyment.
meaning.example: Reading gives me great pleasure.

meaning.definition: Any living animal.
meaning.example: A tiny creature crept under the leaf.

meaning.definition: Different things stirred or put together.
meaning.example: Stir the mixture until it is smooth.

meaning.definition: An exciting journey or experience.
meaning.example: Our camping trip was a big adventure.

meaning.definition: Things like chairs, tables and beds in a room.
meaning.example: We bought new furniture for the lounge.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 — The -sion sound
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -sion that sound like zhun, such as television and decision.

meaning.definition: The ability to see.
meaning.example: The optician checked my vision.

meaning.definition: A choice you make after thinking.
meaning.example: We made a decision to go swimming.

meaning.definition: Sharing or splitting a number into equal groups.
meaning.example: Division is the opposite of multiplication.

meaning.definition: A screen that shows programmes and films.
meaning.example: We watched a funny film on television.

meaning.definition: Not being sure what is happening or what to do.
meaning.example: There was confusion when the lights went out.

meaning.definition: A sudden, loud burst, like a firework.
meaning.example: We heard a loud explosion of fireworks.

meaning.definition: The end of something, or what you decide after thinking.
meaning.example: The story has a happy conclusion.

meaning.definition: When two moving things crash into each other.
meaning.example: The two bumper cars had a gentle collision.

meaning.definition: Watching over people to keep them safe.
meaning.example: Children may only swim with adult supervision.

meaning.definition: Looking over work again to learn it well.
meaning.example: Revision helped me learn my spellings.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 — The -ous ending
chapters.description: Our examples of describing words that end in -ous, such as nervous and dangerous.

meaning.definition: A little worried or afraid about something.
meaning.example: Sam felt nervous before the school play.

meaning.definition: Not joking; important and needing care.
meaning.example: Dad had a serious look on his face.

meaning.definition: Keen to find out or learn about things.
meaning.example: The curious puppy sniffed every corner.

meaning.definition: Wanting something that someone else has.
meaning.example: Ben felt jealous of his friend's new bike.

meaning.definition: Happy to give or share with others.
meaning.example: My gran is generous with her biscuits.

meaning.definition: Likely to cause harm.
meaning.example: The icy path was dangerous to walk on.

meaning.definition: Very, very big.
meaning.example: An enormous whale swam past the boat.

meaning.definition: Keen to try new and exciting things.
meaning.example: My adventurous sister always climbs to the very top.

meaning.definition: Strange and hard to explain.
meaning.example: A mysterious box appeared on the doorstep.

meaning.definition: So silly that it makes you laugh.
meaning.example: He wore a ridiculous hat to the party.

chapters.title: Chapter 15 — ch, gue, que and sc
chapters.focus: ch for k and sh, gue, que and sc
chapters.description: Our examples of spellings borrowed from other languages, such as chorus, tongue, unique and science.

meaning.definition: A shop or person that gives out medicines.
meaning.example: Mum went to the chemist for some plasters.

meaning.definition: A group of people singing together.
meaning.example: The chorus sang loudly at the concert.

meaning.definition: A person who cooks food as a job.
meaning.example: The chef baked a huge chocolate cake.

meaning.definition: Something with moving parts that does a job.
meaning.example: The machine washed our muddy clothes.

meaning.definition: The part inside your mouth that helps you taste.
meaning.example: The lolly turned my tongue bright blue.

meaning.definition: One of a kind; like no other.
meaning.example: Every snowflake is unique.

meaning.definition: Learning about the world through looking and testing.
meaning.example: In science we grew beans in pots.

meaning.definition: A tool with two blades for cutting paper.
meaning.example: Please pass me the scissors and glue.

meaning.definition: A person or animal in a story.
meaning.example: My favourite character in the book is a fox.

meaning.definition: A special way of doing something well.
meaning.example: The teacher showed us a new painting technique.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 — Everyday foundations
chapters.description: A gentle start with shorter but unusual everyday words.

meaning.definition: Difficult or uncomfortable.
meaning.example: It was an awkward silence at the table.

meaning.definition: The number 40.
meaning.example: There are forty children in the hall.

meaning.definition: A picture or sign that stands for something.
meaning.example: A heart is a symbol of love.

meaning.definition: A set of things that work together.
meaning.example: The solar system has eight planets.

meaning.definition: When words end with the same sound, like cat and hat.
meaning.example: Cat and hat are a rhyme.

meaning.definition: A regular pattern of sounds or beats.
meaning.example: Clap to the rhythm of the music.

meaning.definition: A boat used for sailing or racing.
meaning.example: We saw a yacht in the harbour.

meaning.definition: A line of people waiting for something.
meaning.example: We joined the queue for ice cream.

meaning.definition: The parts inside your body that help you move.
meaning.example: Lifting weights builds muscle.

meaning.definition: A dark mark on your skin from being hit.
meaning.example: She had a bruise on her knee after falling.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 — Silent & unusual letters
chapters.description: Words containing silent letters or surprising spellings — the 'gh' in 'thorough', the 'lf' in 'twelfth'.

meaning.definition: The feeling inside that tells you right from wrong.
meaning.example: His conscience told him to say sorry.

meaning.definition: Awake and aware of what is happening.
meaning.example: She was conscious throughout the journey.

meaning.definition: A person who fights for their country.
meaning.example: The soldier stood at attention.

meaning.definition: The part of your body where food goes after you eat.
meaning.example: My stomach hurts because I ate too much.

meaning.definition: Done carefully and completely.
meaning.example: She did a thorough job of cleaning.

meaning.definition: Number 12 in a list or order.
meaning.example: December is the twelfth month.

meaning.definition: From another country.
meaning.example: I am learning a foreign language.

meaning.definition: Someone who lives near you.
meaning.example: Our neighbour brought us some apples.

meaning.definition: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm.
meaning.example: Lightning lit up the dark sky.

meaning.definition: Free time when you are not working.
meaning.example: She spends her leisure time painting.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 — Double consonants
chapters.description: Many words double a consonant — learn to spot when and which.

meaning.definition: To have enough space for someone or something.
meaning.example: The hotel can accommodate two hundred guests.

meaning.definition: To go somewhere with someone.
meaning.example: A teacher will accompany us on the trip.

meaning.definition: As stated by; following.
meaning.example: According to the map, we go left.

meaning.definition: Acting in an angry, fierce way.
meaning.example: The aggressive dog barked at the postman.

meaning.definition: To make someone feel shy or ashamed.
meaning.example: Tripping in front of class can embarrass you.

meaning.definition: To bother someone over and over again.
meaning.example: Please don't harass your sister.

meaning.definition: To fill a space or take someone's time.
meaning.example: Toys can occupy a baby for hours.

meaning.definition: To happen.
meaning.example: Storms occur in autumn.

meaning.definition: A group of people chosen to make decisions together.
meaning.example: The school committee planned the fair.

meaning.definition: Needed to be done.
meaning.example: It is necessary to wash your hands before meals.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 — More doubles & 'equ' family
chapters.description: Further double-letter patterns, plus the 'equ' family (equip, equipped, equipment).

meaning.definition: To be grateful for something; to value it.
meaning.example: I really appreciate your help.

meaning.definition: Joined or fastened to something.
meaning.example: A label was attached to the suitcase.

meaning.definition: To share ideas or messages with others.
meaning.example: We communicate by talking or writing.

meaning.definition: To say something is bigger or more than it really is.
meaning.example: He likes to exaggerate his stories.

meaning.definition: To give someone the things they need.
meaning.example: We equip the team with new boots.

meaning.definition: Given the things needed (past tense of equip).
meaning.example: The climbers were equipped with ropes.

meaning.definition: The things you need for a particular activity.
meaning.example: Sports equipment includes balls and bats.

meaning.definition: To stop someone while they are talking or doing something.
meaning.example: Please don't interrupt me while I am reading.

meaning.definition: To get in the way of something.
meaning.example: Don't interfere with the experiment.

meaning.definition: To put forward an idea.
meaning.example: May I suggest going to the park?

chapters.title: Chapter 5 — Endings: -ent & -ence
chapters.description: These endings follow rules tied to root words — see Appendix 1.

meaning.definition: Something that makes life easier.
meaning.example: A microwave is a great convenience.

meaning.definition: Being real; living.
meaning.example: The existence of dragons is just a story.

meaning.definition: Very good indeed.
meaning.example: She did excellent work in art class.

meaning.definition: Often.
meaning.example: We frequently visit Grandma.

meaning.definition: Enough.
meaning.example: Make sure there is sufficient water.

meaning.definition: Very old, from long ago.
meaning.example: We saw ancient ruins in Rome.

meaning.definition: Easy to see or understand; obvious.
meaning.example: It was apparent that he was tired.

meaning.definition: Connected to what is being discussed.
meaning.example: Please give a relevant answer.

meaning.definition: Something that gets in the way.
meaning.example: The heavy bag was a hindrance on the walk.

meaning.definition: Something or someone annoying.
meaning.example: The buzzing fly was a real nuisance.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Endings: -ate, -ise & long words
chapters.description: Verbs ending in -ate, -ise, and other long words built from common roots.

meaning.definition: To say what is wrong with something.
meaning.example: Try not to criticise others unkindly.

meaning.definition: To know who someone is when you see them.
meaning.example: I didn't recognise you with your new hair!

meaning.definition: Giving something up for someone else.
meaning.example: Her parents made sacrifices for her education.

meaning.definition: Sure; without any doubt.
meaning.example: We have a definite answer at last.

meaning.definition: Feeling so worried you will try anything.
meaning.example: He was desperate to find his lost dog.

meaning.definition: Happening right now without waiting.
meaning.example: I need an immediate answer please.

meaning.definition: Right away, without delay.
meaning.example: Stop immediately when I shout stop.

meaning.definition: A test of who is best at something.
meaning.example: She won the spelling competition.

meaning.definition: Saying what something means or why it happened.
meaning.example: Please give an explanation for your lateness.

meaning.definition: The way a word is said.
meaning.example: Practise the pronunciation of new words.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — Greek & foreign-origin words
chapters.description: Words borrowed from Greek, French and Latin — they don't always follow English rules.

meaning.definition: Someone who does something for fun, not as a job.
meaning.example: He is an amateur photographer.

meaning.definition: A car, bus, lorry or other machine for transport.
meaning.example: A bus is a large vehicle.

meaning.definition: The words people use to talk to each other.
meaning.example: English is my favourite language.

meaning.definition: A place where you can buy and eat meals.
meaning.example: We went to a restaurant for my birthday.

meaning.definition: A group of things that are alike.
meaning.example: Apples and pears are in the fruit category.

meaning.definition: A place where dead people are buried.
meaning.example: The old cemetery had stone monuments.

meaning.definition: A book that lists words and tells you what they mean.
meaning.example: Look up the word in a dictionary.

meaning.definition: A big disagreement that lots of people argue about.
meaning.example: The new rule caused a lot of controversy.

meaning.definition: A person who helps in an office with letters and appointments.
meaning.example: The secretary booked the meeting.

meaning.definition: To do with the body.
meaning.example: PE means physical education.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Schwa & vowel traps
chapters.description: Words where an unstressed vowel sounds like 'uh' — easy to misspell. Learn the parent word!

meaning.definition: Well known to you.
meaning.example: Her face looked familiar but I forgot her name.

meaning.definition: How hot or cold something is.
meaning.example: The doctor took my temperature.

meaning.definition: Your name written your own special way.
meaning.example: Please put your signature on the form.

meaning.definition: To make someone agree to do something.
meaning.example: Can you persuade her to come too?

meaning.definition: Wanting to know about things.
meaning.example: Her curiosity led her to read every book.

meaning.definition: Normal; in the middle, not too high or low.
meaning.example: He is of average height for his age.

meaning.definition: To grow or get better over time.
meaning.example: Plants develop from tiny seeds.

meaning.definition: The world around us and all of nature.
meaning.example: We must protect the environment.

meaning.definition: The part of your body where your arm joins.
meaning.example: He carried his bag on his shoulder.

meaning.definition: To do something well after trying hard.
meaning.example: She worked hard to achieve good marks.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — Tricky everyday long words
chapters.description: Long words used often in writing — worth learning thoroughly.

meaning.definition: A group of people living together in one place.
meaning.example: Our community held a summer fair.

meaning.definition: The group of people who run a country.
meaning.example: The government makes the laws.

meaning.definition: One single person.
meaning.example: Every individual matters.

meaning.definition: Wonderful or amazing.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 — Final hardest set
chapters.description: The toughest words on the Year 5/6 list — once you can spell these, you can spell anything.

meaning.definition: Something bought cheaply; a good deal.

meaning.example: The two children correspond by email.

meaning.example: She was determined to win the race.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 — Words ending -cious and -tious
chapters.description: Words that end with a 'shus' sound spelt -cious or -tious; our examples show which fits.

meaning.definition: Very cruel and fierce, ready to hurt.
meaning.example: In the story, a vicious troll guarded the bridge.

meaning.example: She kept the precious ring in a small box.

meaning.example: The dog gave the new cat a suspicious sniff.

meaning.example: Her laugh was so infectious that we all joined in.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 — Words ending -cial and -tial
chapters.description: Words that end with a 'shul' sound spelt -cial or -tial; our examples show which fits.

meaning.definition: Connected with meeting and spending time with other people.
meaning.example: The club holds a social evening every Friday.

meaning.definition: To do with buying, selling and business.

meaning.example: The young player has great potential.

meaning.example: The shop sold artificial flowers that never die.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 — Words ending -ant, -ance and -ancy
chapters.description: Words ending in -ant, -ance or -ancy, where the vowel sound is hard to hear; our examples show the rule.

meaning.definition: Far away in space or time.
meaning.example: We could see distant hills through the mist.

meaning.definition: Happening straight away, with no waiting.
meaning.example: The magic trick was an instant success.

meaning.definition: Nice, enjoyable and friendly.
meaning.example: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the river.

meaning.definition: Graceful and stylish in the way it looks.
meaning.example: The swan looked elegant as it glided past.

meaning.example: The distance from here to school is a mile.

meaning.example: She kept her balance on the narrow wall.

meaning.definition: How much something matters.
meaning.example: The teacher explained the importance of good manners.

meaning.example: Our class had the best attendance this term.

meaning.example: The hotel had a vacancy for one night.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 — Words ending -able and -ably
chapters.description: Words ending in -able or -ably, which are often added to a whole word; our examples show the rule.

meaning.definition: Worth a lot of money or very useful.

meaning.definition: So sweet and lovely that everyone wants to cuddle it.
meaning.example: The adorable puppy wagged its tail.

meaning.definition: In a way that is surprising and worth noticing.

meaning.definition: Giving you pleasure and fun.
meaning.example: We had an enjoyable day at the seaside.

meaning.definition: Fair and sensible.

meaning.definition: Popular and in style at the moment.
meaning.example: She wore a fashionable hat to the party.

meaning.example: The cat slept comfortably on the warm rug.

meaning.definition: In a fair and sensible way.
meaning.example: The new bike was reasonably cheap.

meaning.definition: The person who makes sure players keep to the rules.

meaning.definition: Liking one thing better than another.

meaning.definition: Liked one thing better than another.
meaning.example: We preferred the red kite to the green one.

meaning.definition: Liking one thing better than another.
meaning.example: Preferring the quiet seat, he sat by the window.

meaning.example: The photos were transferred onto the new computer.

meaning.example: Dad is transferring the water into a jug.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 — ei after c

meaning.definition: Got or was given something.

meaning.definition: The part of a telephone that you hold to your ear.

meaning.example: The fox tried to deceive the little hen.

meaning.example: The story was about a cruel trick and deceit.

meaning.definition: Too proud of yourself and your own cleverness.

meaning.example: The deceitful pirate hid the map in his coat.

meaning.definition: To notice or understand something.
meaning.example: I could perceive a faint light in the distance.

meaning.example: Can you conceive of a world without colour?

chapters.title: Chapter 12 — ough words
chapters.description: Our examples of words with the tricky letters ough, which can sound many different ways.

meaning.definition: The joint in the middle of your leg.
